plan.hypothesis: H0: all k=3 group means are equal; H1: at least one group mean differs
assumptions: Population eta-squared η² = 0.08 reflects true effect size
scientific_notes: Eta-squared (η²) is the proportion of total variance explained by the grouping factor
For fixed effects ANOVA, η² relates to the noncentrality parameter λ via λ = n × k × (η² / (1 - η²))
Power is computed as P(F_{k-1, N-k}(λ) > F_crit) using the noncentral F-distribution
k=3 groups, N=75 total, so df_between=2, df_within=72

answer.summary: For a balanced one-way fixed effects ANOVA with 3 independent normal groups, total sample size 75 (25 per group), population eta-squared 0.08, and significance level α = 0.05, the omnibus F-test power is **0.603118 probability** (approximately 60.3%).
answer.method: Fixed effects one-way ANOVA omnibus F-test power using noncentral F-distribution. The noncentrality parameter λ is computed from the per-group sample size (n=25), number of groups (k=3), and population eta-squared (η²=0.08) via λ = n·k·(η²/(1−η²)) = 6.5217. The critical F-value at α=0.05 with df₁=2 and df₂=72 is F_crit = 3.1239. Power is P(F_{2,72}(λ=6.5217) > 3.1239) evaluated using the noncentral F cumulative distribution function.
assumptions: Fixed effects one-way ANOVA with balanced design
3 independent groups with equal sample sizes (n=25 per group)
Observations within each group are normally distributed
Common variance across all groups (homogeneity of variance)
Population eta-squared η²=0.08 represents the true effect size in the population
Omnibus null hypothesis: all k=3 group means are equal
One-sided test (directional): alternative hypothesis that at least one group mean differs
limitations: Result applies only to the omnibus F-test, not to post-hoc pairwise comparisons or specific contrasts
Assumes normality and homogeneity of variance; violations may affect actual power
Eta-squared depends on allocation of effects across groups; balanced power assumes no specific pattern
Fixed effects framework; random or mixed effects models would require different calculations
No correction for multiple testing beyond the omnibus test is considered

executions.code:
# Balanced one-way ANOVA power calculation
# Parameters
k <- 3                    # number of groups
N <- 75                   # total sample size
eta_sq <- 0.08           # population eta-squared
alpha <- 0.05            # significance level
n_per_group <- N / k     # participants per group (balanced design)

# Compute degrees of freedom
df_between <- k - 1       # df for numerator
df_within <- N - k        # df for denominator

cat("Design parameters:\n")
cat("  Number of groups (k):", k, "\n")
cat("  Total sample size (N):", N, "\n")
cat("  Sample size per group (n):", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("  Population eta-squared:", eta_sq, "\n")
cat("  Significance level (alpha):", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Degrees of freedom between groups:", df_between, "\n")
cat("  Degrees of freedom within groups:", df_within, "\n\n")

# Compute noncentrality parameter lambda
# For fixed effects ANOVA: lambda = n * k * (eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq))
# where n is per-group sample size
lambda <- n_per_group * k * (eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq))

cat("Noncentrality parameter calculation:\n")
cat("  lambda = n * k * (eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq))\n")
cat("  lambda = ", n_per_group, " * ", k, " * (", eta_sq, " / ", (1 - eta_sq), ")\n")
cat("  lambda = ", lambda, "\n\n")

# Critical F value at alpha level
F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df_between, df_within)

cat("Critical F value:\n")
cat("  F_crit (alpha=", alpha, ", df1=", df_between, ", df2=", df_within, ") = ", F_crit, "\n\n")

# Power = P(F_{df_between, df_within}(lambda) > F_crit)
# Using the noncentral F distribution
power <- 1 - pf(F_crit, df_between, df_within, ncp = lambda)

cat("Power calculation:\n")
cat("  Power = P(F_noncentral(lambda=", lambda, ") > F_crit)\n")
cat("  Power = ", power, "\n\n")

# Format for output
result_power <- round(power, 6)
cat("Final result:\n")
cat("  Omnibus F-test power = ", result_power, "\n")

# Output in structured format
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = power, unit = "probability")
  )),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
))
